title: Check if All A's Appears Before All B's
summary: Determine if all instances of 'a' precede all instances of 'b' in the string s, returning true if so, otherwise false.
statement: Determine if all instances of 'a' precede all instances of 'b' in the string s, returning true if so, otherwise false.
constraints: s is nonempty and contains only a and b.
Return true exactly when no a appears after any b.
Strings containing only one character type satisfy the condition.
reference_solution:
def all_a_before_b(s):
    return 'ba' not in s
hints: Once a b has appeared, any later a creates an adjacent ba boundary somewhere in the string.
The condition is equivalent to forbidding substring ba.
If an a follows any b, the transition from the last preceding b-run to that a contains ba; conversely ba directly violates the order.
editorial: If an a follows any b, the transition from the last preceding b-run to that a contains ba; conversely ba directly violates the order.

tests.explanation: All a characters occur before the first b.
The a at index two occurs after a b, so the condition fails.
